summary: Orchid AI: Suspected routing policy change caused intermittent 5xx (policy evaluation errors) in us-east
description:
Issue summary
- Customer reports intermittent 5xx errors beginning ~2025-02-19 17:05 UTC for chat completions routed to us-east.
- Customer suspects a routing policy change on Redwood side; they did not deploy any client changes.
- Error strings reported by customer include: "policy_eval_error" and occasional "no_healthy_upstream".

Impact
- ~6–12% of requests failing for ~28 minutes (customer-side sampled); elevated p95 latency during same window.
- Customer workloads are production (end-user requests). They observed retries masking some impact but still user-visible.

Environment
- Tenant: Orchid AI (enterprise)
- Region: us-east
- Endpoint: /v1/chat/completions (streaming enabled)
- Models: llama-3.1-70b-instruct primary; llama-3.1-8b-instruct used as fallback by policy

Customer request
- Confirm whether Redwood changed routing/policy configuration around the incident window.
- Provide a "diff" of routing/policy changes that affected their tenant.

Notes / constraints
- We cannot share raw internal policy bundles or tenant routing keys as-is; must provide a sanitized, customer-safe summary.
- This ticket is a motivating example for "safe config diffs" with redaction + audit trail (see ENG-2843).
comments:
2025-02-19 17:22 UTC — Customer (Dana R., Orchid AI)
We’re seeing intermittent 5xx on chat completions in us-east starting ~17:05 UTC. We did not deploy anything today. Errors include `policy_eval_error` and sometimes `no_healthy_upstream`. Can you confirm whether any routing policy changed on your side? If so, can you share what changed?

Sample request id: req_01HPXK3J9Y1… (more available)
Model: redwood/llama-3.1-70b-instruct
Streaming: true

2025-02-19 17:29 UTC — Aisha Bello (Redwood Support)
Thanks—acknowledged. We’re investigating with SRE/Platform now. We’ll confirm whether there were any routing/config changes in the timeframe and will share a customer-safe summary of findings.

A couple quick questions to narrow scope:
1) Are failures confined to us-east or do you see impact in other regions?
2) Are you pinning any model version or using the default alias?
3) Do you have any recent changes to your own retry/backoff settings?

2025-02-19 17:33 UTC — Customer (Dana R., Orchid AI)
Only us-east from what we can tell. We use the default model alias (no explicit version pin). Retries unchanged.

2025-02-19 17:41 UTC — Jacob Stein (Automated Diagnostics / Eng) [INTERNAL]
Pulled initial traces for Orchid tenant in us-east: spike of `policy_eval_error` starting 17:06 UTC, ends ~17:34 UTC. Correlates with control-plane config bundle refresh. The failures look like a policy evaluation exception rather than upstream model failure.

Hypothesis: a routing policy bundle change was applied without tenant scoping and briefly impacted Orchid’s tenant route group.

Action:
- Paging Platform routing on-call for config timeline + any recent rollouts.
- Need exact effective config snapshot at t-30m vs now; current tooling doesn’t provide safe diff quickly (this is exactly the gap in ENG-2843).

2025-02-19 17:48 UTC — Priya Natarajan (Platform) [INTERNAL]
Found a policy bundle publish at 17:04 UTC (bundle_version=2025.02.19.1704) that included a change to default fallback constraints. It should have been scoped to an internal route group but appears to have matched a broader selector due to missing tenant guard.

Rollback initiated: reverting to previous bundle_version=2025.02.19.1620 in us-east.
ETA 5–10 min for full propagation.

2025-02-19 17:55 UTC — Aisha Bello (Redwood Support)
Update: We identified an internal routing configuration change that likely correlates with your error window in us-east. The team is rolling it back now to restore expected behavior. Next update in ~10 minutes with confirmation of stabilization.

Separately, we’re preparing a sanitized summary of what changed (we can’t share raw internal policy configs verbatim, but we will share the portion relevant to your tenant impact).

2025-02-19 18:07 UTC — Ethan Park (Control Plane TL) [INTERNAL]
Rollback complete; error rate back to baseline. Root cause: selector condition used `route_group != "restricted"` when it should have been `route_group == "internal-test"`. This inadvertently applied a stricter fallback constraint to more tenants, including Orchid, causing policy eval failures in a small subset of requests that hit the affected branch.

Follow-ups:
- Add guardrail validation in policy publisher (prevent broad selectors without explicit allowlist).
- Need customer-safe diff mechanism + redaction (ENG-2843) and effective config snapshot endpoint performance/caching (PR 18436).

2025-02-19 18:12 UTC — Aisha Bello (Redwood Support)
We’ve rolled back a routing configuration change in us-east and are seeing error rates return to baseline on our side.

Customer-safe summary of what changed:
- A routing policy update published around 17:04 UTC unintentionally broadened its matching scope.
- For some requests, this caused the router to evaluate a fallback rule incorrectly, resulting in `policy_eval_error` (and in a smaller number of cases, `no_healthy_upstream`).
- We reverted the change by ~18:05 UTC and have confirmed recovery.

If you can share ~5 additional request IDs from the window (17:05–17:35 UTC), we can confirm they align with the same policy path.

2025-02-19 18:19 UTC — Customer (Dana R., Orchid AI)
Confirmed: failures stopped. Here are 6 request IDs from 17:10–17:22 UTC: req_… (list redacted here). Please keep us posted on prevention steps. Also, we’d still like a diff of what policy changed for our tenant if that’s possible.

2025-02-20 09:03 UTC — Marcus Lin (Security) [INTERNAL]
Reminder: do not paste raw policy bundle contents into a customer-visible ticket. Approved approach: provide a narrative summary + non-sensitive key names only if allowlisted. For any config diffs, ensure keys and values are classified “safe-to-post” and log access in audit trail.

Recommendation: route customer requests for diffs through the new redaction path being built under ENG-2843; until then, keep it high-level.

2025-02-20 10:26 UTC — Jacob Stein (Automated Diagnostics / Eng) [INTERNAL]
Validated the 6 request IDs: all hit the affected policy branch. I’m adding this ticket as a concrete example to ENG-2843 acceptance criteria: responders need a one-click sanitized diff of effective routing policy (t-30m vs now) with strict redaction.

Also linking ENG-2846 (event schema) so we can annotate policy publishes on the change correlation dashboard.

2025-02-20 10:45 UTC — Aisha Bello (Redwood Support)
On the “diff” request: today we can’t provide a raw config diff export (it would expose internal routing details and other sensitive keys). However, we can provide the relevant effective-behavior change summary:
- The change altered a fallback-selection condition and broadened which requests were evaluated under that condition.
- This led to an evaluation exception for a subset of requests, producing the errors you observed.
- We have reverted the change and are implementing guardrails so broad selectors cannot be published without explicit scoping.

We’re also implementing internal tooling to generate safe, redacted config diffs for faster incident communication going forward (so we can answer this class of question with more precision without leaking sensitive details).

2025-02-21 16:18 UTC — Customer (Dana R., Orchid AI)
Understood. Please share when the guardrails are live. If there’s any customer-facing way to subscribe to routing change notifications for our tenant, we’d be interested.

2025-02-22 11:32 UTC — Aisha Bello (Redwood Support)
Guardrail work is in progress (internal validation on policy publishes + improved change annotations). We don’t currently have tenant-scoped routing change notifications exposed to customers, but we’ve captured this as feedback.

We’ll close this ticket as resolved since service is stable; if you see any recurrence, reply here with request IDs and timestamps and we’ll re-open immediately.
resolution: Resolved via rollback of an unintended routing policy selector broadening in us-east. Recovery confirmed by Redwood metrics and customer confirmation. Follow-up actions tracked internally: safe/redacted config diff tooling (ENG-2843), standardized change annotation event schema (ENG-2846), and policy publish guardrails in control plane.
